transcript.message: Hi Priya, this is Era calling from Outsourcy. I know this is out of the blue, do you have thirty seconds and then you can tell me to get lost?

I saw Loomward has had a marketing operations role open for about three weeks, sixty to seventy thousand. We place dedicated full-time marketing ops people who work your hours from our office, at about a third of that fully loaded. Before I say anything else, how is the search going?
Honestly, slow. We've interviewed two people and neither was great, so, yeah. And I'm in the middle of a website relaunch so it keeps slipping.
Two interviews in three weeks while you're relaunching the site. What's falling on you in the meantime, the HubSpot side or the reporting?
Both! The workflows, the webinar follow-up, and Sam wants a report every Monday. My content person is amazing at writing and not an ops person, so it's me at night.

That is exactly the seat we fill. One person, full time, only Loomward, working nine to five Eastern from our office in Pristina with a manager on the floor. You interview them and pick. The way we start is simple: give me a ten-minute brief and in about seventy-two hours you get two or three profiles with short video interviews. Nothing owed until you choose someone.
Oh that sounds amazing, honestly. I'd probably have to run it by Sam though. Could you send me some info?

Of course, and I'll make it easy for Sam. Let's do this: I send the profiles by Thursday, and you and I take fifteen minutes Friday to go through them, and if you want Sam on it I'll put him on the invite. Friday at ten or at two, which is better?
Um, Friday at two works. And yeah, add Sam, that's probably smart.
Friday at two Eastern, fifteen minutes, you and Sam, profiles in your inbox Thursday. What's the best email for the invite?
priya at loomward dot com. This is great, thank you!
